**Summary (for your article):**  
Recent data show that roughly **one in three people in Senegal experiences moderate or severe food insecurity**, while around **7% face high levels of acute food insecurity**. Food prices have risen sharply since 2022, and average protein availability remains modest.

---

## Data

### 1. Prevalence of food insecurity (FAO – experience‑based FIES indicators)

**a) Severe food insecurity (SDG 2.1.2 component)**  
Indicator: *Prevalence of severe food insecurity in the total population (percent, 3‑year average)* — FAO, FIES.

- 2022–2024 (labeled 2024):  
  - Central estimate: <claim id="db287b1b" policy="auto">4</claim>% of the population  
  - 90% confidence interval: <claim id="d5c8742b" policy="auto">2.9</claim>% – <claim id="3ee81925" policy="auto">5.1</claim>%

Trend (3‑year averages, central estimate):  

| 3‑year base period | Labeled year | Severe food insecurity (% of population) |
|--------------------|-------------|------------------------------------------|

| 2018–2020          | 2020        | <claim id="213dd599" policy="auto">6</claim>%   |
| 2019–2021          | 2021        | <claim id="67b9459d" policy="auto">5.1</claim>% |
| 2020–2022          | 2022        | <claim id="0b921843" policy="auto">4.5</claim>% |
| 2021–2023          | 2023        | <claim id="0bc9f112" policy="auto">4</claim>%   |
| 2022–2024          | 2024        | <claim id="db287b1b" policy="auto">4</claim>%   |

**b) Moderate or severe food insecurity (SDG 2.1.2 headline)**  
Indicator: *Prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity in the total population (percent, 3‑year average)* — FAO, FIES.

- 2022–2024 (labeled 2024):  
  - Central estimate: <claim id="f1ef9b51" policy="auto">29.1</claim>% of the population  
  - 90% confidence interval: <claim id="42d91154" policy="auto">26.8</claim>% – <claim id="4b0ffd39" policy="auto">31.3</claim>%

Trend (3‑year averages, central estimate):  

| 3‑year base period | Labeled year | Moderate or severe food insecurity (%) |
|--------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|
| 2017–2019          | 2019        | <claim id="93df6e7f" policy="auto">35.1</claim>% |

| 2022–2024          | 2024        | <claim id="f1ef9b51" policy="auto">29.1</claim>% |

**c) Number of people affected (FAO, 3‑year averages)**  

- Severely food insecure people (3‑year average, millions):  
  - 2022–2024 (labeled 2024): <claim id="4a6ff2e1" policy="auto">0.7</claim> million people  
    - 90% CI: <claim id="d2ed0f90" policy="auto">0.5</claim> – <claim id="9b003d53" policy="auto">0.9</claim> million  

- Moderately or severely food insecure people (3‑year average, millions):  
  - 2022–2024 (labeled 2024): <claim id="df969bec" policy="auto">5.3</claim> million people  
    - 90% CI: <claim id="57f3bf78" policy="auto">4.8</claim> – <claim id="4973f95b" policy="auto">5.7</claim> million  

(FAO uses a **unit multiplier of 10⁶**, so these are millions.)

### 2. Acute food insecurity – “Crisis or worse” (IPC Phase 3+)  

Indicator: *Population facing high levels of acute food insecurity (IPC/CH Phase 3 or above)* — FSIN/GRFC.

You can safely quote formulations like:

1. **Chronic food access (moderate/severe):**  
   - “According to FAO’s Food Insecurity Experience Scale, about **three in ten people in Senegal — roughly 29% of the population — lived in households experiencing moderate or severe food insecurity over 2022–2024** (3‑year average).”  
     (Central estimate <claim id="f1ef9b51" policy="auto">29.1</claim>%, 90% CI <claim id="42d91154" policy="auto">26.8</claim>%–<claim id="4b0ffd39" policy="auto">31.3</claim>%.)

2. **Severe deprivation:**  
   - “An estimated **4% of Senegal’s population — around 700,000 people — faced severe food insecurity in 2022–2024**, meaning adults in their households sometimes had to skip meals, eat much less, or go a whole day without eating.”  
     (Prevalence <claim id="db287b1b" policy="auto">4</claim>%; absolute number <claim id="4a6ff2e1" policy="auto">0.7</claim> million, 90% CI <claim id="d2ed0f90" policy="auto">0.5</claim>–<claim id="9b003d53" policy="auto">0.9</claim> million.)

3. **Wider food access problem (moderate+severe):**  
   - “FAO estimates that **around 5.3 million people in Senegal were moderately or severely food insecure in 2022–2024**, out of a total population of about 18–19 million.”  
     (Number <claim id="df969bec" policy="auto">5.3</claim> million, 90% CI <claim id="57f3bf78" policy="auto">4.8</claim>–<claim id="4973f95b" policy="auto">5.7</claim> million.)

4. **Trend since late 2010s:**  
   - “The share of people in Senegal facing moderate or severe food insecurity has fallen from about **35% in 2017–2019** to about **29% in 2022–2024**, but remains high.”  
     (From <claim id="93df6e7f" policy="auto">35.1</claim>% to <claim id="f1ef9b51" policy="auto">29.1</claim>%.)

5. **Acute food crises (IPC Phase 3+):**  
   - “The Food Security Information Network estimates that in **2023, roughly 1.26 million people in Senegal — just over 7% of the population — were in IPC Phase 3 or worse (‘Crisis’ or higher) acute food insecurity.**”  
     (Share <claim id="890111ee" policy="auto">7.06696</claim>%; people <claim id="df989469" policy="auto">1,263,290</claim>.)

   - “The number of people in acute food crisis has more than tripled since 2019, rising from around **360,000 people** to over **1.26 million** in 2023.”  
     (From <claim id="8d305c0d" policy="auto">359,646</claim> to <claim id="df989469" policy="auto">1,263,290</claim>.)

6. **Food prices shock:**  
   - “Food prices surged in Senegal in 2022: FAO data show food price inflation peaking at **about 21% year‑on‑year in November 2022**, compared with low single digits before the pandemic.”  
     (November 2022: <claim id="71d6e9fc" policy="auto">21.403038</claim>%; January 2021: <claim id="7e6921ae" policy="auto">0.542986</claim>%.)

7. **Diet quality proxy (protein supply):**  
   - “Average protein availability in Senegal has inched up from around **66 grams per person per day in 2017–2019** to about **70 grams in 2020–2022**, according to FAO food balance sheets.”  
     (From <claim id="d33a933c" policy="auto">66.1</claim> g to <claim id="3a672c1d" policy="auto">69.5</claim> g per capita per day.)

indicator_metadata.name: Prevalence of severe food insecurity in the total population (percent) (3-year average)
indicator_metadata.measurement_unit: Percentage, Upper Bound for the 90% confidence interval, Lower Bound for the 90% confidence interval
indicator_metadata.definition_long:
The prevalence of severe food insecurity is an estimate of the percentage of people in the population who live in households classified as severely food insecure.
The assessment is conducted using data collected with the Food Insecurity Experience Scale or a compatible experience-based food security measurement questionnaire (such as the HFSSM).
The probability to be food insecure is estimated using the one-parameter logistic Item Response Theory model (the Rasch model) and thresholds for classification are made cross country comparable by calibrating the metrics obtained in each country against the FIES global reference scale, maintained by FAO. The threshold to classify "severe" food insecurity corresponds to the severity associated with the item "having not eaten for an entire day" on the global FIES scale.
In simpler terms, a household is classified as severely food insecure when at least one adult in the household has reported to have been exposed, at times during the year, to several of the most severe experiences described in the FIES questions, such as to have been forced to reduce the quantity of the food, to have skipped meals, having gone hungry, or having to go for a whole day without eating because of a lack of money or other resources. 
It is an indicator of lack of food access.
Confidence intervals at 90% level are also available. They are computed considering both sampling and measurement variability.
indicator_metadata.methodology:
More details on the methodology for computing the prevalence of severe food insecurity are in "Methods for estimating comparable prevalence rates of food insecurity experienced by adults throughout the world", Voices of the Hungry Technical Report N. 1, April 2016 (http://www.fao.org/3/c-i4830e.pdf ).
See also the metadata document at https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/files/Metadata-02-02-01.pdf.
indicator_metadata.relevance: This is indicator 2.1.2 in the SDG framework, to monitor target 2.1 ("By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, […], to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round").
indicator_metadata.aggregation_method: The aggregates are computed using a weighted population average.
indicator_metadata.confidentiality: This work is made available under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/igo/). In addition to this license, some database specific terms of use are listed: Terms of Use of Datasets (https://www.fao.org/contact-us/terms/db-terms-of-use/en/).

The prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity is an estimate of the percentage of people in the population who live in households classified as moderately or severely food insecure.
The assessment is conducted using data collected with the Food Insecurity Experience Scale or a compatible experience-based food security measurement questionnaire (such as the HFSSM).

In simpler terms, a household is classified as moderately or severely food insecure when at least one adult in the household has reported to have been exposed, at times during the year, to low quality diets and might have been forced to also reduce the quantity of food they would normally eat because of a lack of money or other resources. 
It is an indicator of lack of food access.
Confidence intervals at 90% level are also available. They are computed considering both sampling and measurement variability.

---

**Data:**

- Moderate or severe food insecurity (3‑year average prevalence, % of population, FAO FIES):  
  - 2019 (2017–2019): <claim id="93df6e7f" policy="auto">35.1</claim>%  
  - 2020 (2018–2020): <claim id="b7630a10" policy="auto">33.3</claim>%  
  - 2021 (2019–2021): <claim id="2c1b2005" policy="auto">31.6</claim>%  
  - 2022 (2020–2022): <claim id="58923872" policy="auto">30.3</claim>%  
  - 2023 (2021–2023): <claim id="7faf73b0" policy="auto">29.4</claim>%  
  - 2024 (2022–2024): <claim id="f1ef9b51" policy="auto">29.1</claim>%

- Population in IPC Phase 3+ (Crisis or worse acute food insecurity, FSIN/GRFC):  
  - 2019: <claim id="8d305c0d" policy="auto">359,646</claim> people  
  - 2020: <claim id="2dd6af1b" policy="auto">766,725</claim> people  
  - 2021: <claim id="70c9aa3e" policy="auto">488,048</claim> people  
  - 2022: <claim id="1781bbeb" policy="auto">881,276</claim> people

---

**Analysis (how to visualize it):**

### 1. Chart 1 – Trend in moderate or severe food insecurity (%)

Use this as a **line chart** with one series:

- **X‑axis:** Year (2019–2024; remember each point is a 3‑year average).
